recipes.name: Walnut-Tarragon Chicken Tenders
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast, cut into thin strips

steps.text: Beat the egg together with the milk in a shallow bowl. Combine the walnuts, flour, tarragon, and salt in a second shallow bowl. Dip the chicken strips first into the egg mixture, then into the flour mixture, coating evenly, and place on a plate.

Melt the butter with the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in small batches in the butter mixture until the coating is browned and crispy, about 5 minutes. Test one to be sure it is cooked through. Chicken should be no longer pink and juices run clear. Drain on paper towels.

raw_recipe.headline: Walnut-Tarragon Chicken Tenders
raw_recipe.description: Combining walnuts for crunch and tarragon for subtle flavor, these chicken tenders offer appealing taste and texture all ages will enjoy.

review.reviewBody: Really quick and really easy! To try and make the recipe a little healthier, I used only the egg white and skim milk. I also put in more a little more walnut and went light on the flour (to cut carbs and up the protein) And finally I omitted the butter and just used olive oil. I really just love how crisp the breading gets and how juicy the chicken stays!

I just made this for lunch and it was delicious! I substituted 1 cup of fat free half and half for the milk and since I had egg beaters, I used 1/4 cup of those instead of the egg. I also dipped half of the tenders twice in the two mixtures because I had so much left over and they were really crunchy and very good as well. Thanks for the great easy recipe, Dusty!

Great recipe! I used frozen grilled chicken strips which I cooked according to the package instructions (3 minutes in the microwave). It made frying the chicken much easier as I already knew the chicken was cooked.
Used whole wheat flour and only olive oil no butter. Husband, who is diabetic loved it and so did I.

This is my new FAVORITE chicken recipe! I made my tenders very thin and used a bladed-meat tenderizer, because I am very particular about my chicken consistency. I made the mistake of not chopping the walnuts small enough, which made breading a bit messy. Next time I'll fine-chop my walnuts and this recipe will be absolutely superb. Thanks!

Awesome recipe!! I love it when fabulous cooks enhance my repertoire of cooking--especially chicken! We all just loved the nutty flavor combo of the walnuts and tarragon. Who ever thinks of tarragon when seasoning food? I do now! Here's what I did to make the recipe more heart-healthy: used spelt flour, walnut oil and fresh tarragon. Also used lowfat milk. This is a keeper and will definitely make it again!

I never really think about using tarragon in recipes, but this was perfect! I tried to health-ify the recipe a little by cutting out the butter and frying in olive oil instead of vegetable, and the flavor was wonderful! A great recipe. Thank you for sharing!

This recipe was good but next time instead of using cow's milk I'd substitute almond milk and possibly crushed almonds and almond flour for the breading. I liked the subtle tarragon flavor blended with the nutty flavor. It's a keeper!

my review is only 3, dredged in seasoned flour first then egg wash then in pecan crumbs and panko, pecan was to large needs to be fine crumbs otherwise was great, the original recipe was a 5 except should dredge in flour fie=rst , it makes the rest stick better
This recipe is wonderful. I used cashews instead of walnuts, and my son who hates nuts ate everything on his plate and went back for seconds! Highly recommend this recipe to everyone!
Very easy to make and so very tasty. I only had chicken tenders so adjusted the amounts for smaller amount but it was delicious
Yes! I would make this again. I love tarragon.
I found it necessary to at least double the tarragon for the flavor I was looking for but otherwise an excellent recipe and quite easy.
Good, but needs a little something, so I made a milk gravy from the frying oil and the little bit of flour mixture that was left. Y'all. Do that. Seriously.
Have 3 kids. They just love it!!!!!!!!!!!!

i don't exactly know how i feel about this dish.. i think the walnut coating was just a little too different for me.. loved the tarragon in this though.. ended up squeezing some lemon over the chicken.. still undecided

I used my moule to grind up the walnuts, and I think the size was too small because the taste of the walnuts pretty much got lost in the flour (maybe there was too much flour for this?). I followed the recipe exactly, and it made for a nice dinner, but our leftovers really didn't cut it. I will try this again but make the changes that I have written about. Thanks for the idea!

This is the best chicken tender recipe I have ever made. My husband, and two teenaged kids loved them. The tenders came out most and had a good crunch. I used cashews instead of walnuts, cause that's what I had in the pantry.
our family did not care for this - it was ok
